title: Per-model & per-route performance dashboard: prototype, chart spec, and review notes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and specification for per-model and per-route performance dashboards in Redwood Console. Deliverables: high-fidelity prototype (Figma), chart specification for engineering, interaction patterns for time-range sync / compare, accessibility and labeling guidelines, and a short roll-forward plan for telemetry needs. Goal: give platform users (SREs, platform engineers, product teams) fast insight into latency, throughput, token metrics, and cost-per-token across model versions and HTTP routes. This ticket captures design decisions, trade-offs, and reviewer feedback from PM and Eng.
chart_specs: Primary dashboard cards: Overall RPS (requests/s), Aggregate tokens/sec, Errors/s, Average token cost (USD per 1k tokens). Each card shows current value + delta vs baseline period.

Time-series panel: Multi-line chart with selectable percentiles for latency (p50, p90, p95, p99). Default display: p50 (solid), p95 (dashed), p99 (dot). Provide percentile shading option: band between p50 and p95.
Throughput & concurrency: Stacked area for successful vs failed requests; overlay bar for concurrent in-flight requests. Aggregation window defaults to 1m with rollups available at 5m and 1h.
Token metrics: Dual-axis chart showing input tokens (left, area), output tokens (left, area stacked), and tokens/sec (right, line). Tooltip includes median prompt_length and response_length.
Per-route small multiples: Grid of sparklines (one per route) showing p95 latency over selected time range. Clicking a sparkline opens route detail with full chart set and top example traces.
Heatmap: Model-version vs route latency heatmap (color = p95 latency). Sortable by any metric; supports k-means-style clustering to surface hotpaths.
Distribution panel: Latency histogram with adjustable binning; option to switch to log scale when p99/p50 ratio > 20.
Cost breakdown: Waterfall chart showing contribution to total token cost by model, route, and user-level quota buckets. Include per-1M-token normalized cost metric for quick comparisons.
Annotations: Show deployment/rollout events as vertical bands. Canary overlays appear semi-transparent; users can toggle to highlight canary vs baseline requests.
Export & deep-dive: CSV export of visible time window; link to tracing view for selected time slice and example request ids shown in tooltips.
Axis & UX rules: X-axis uses UTC by default, user-configurable timezone. Y-axis auto-scale with option to pin max. Provide log scale choice on latency charts.
Interaction patterns: Time-range sync across all panels by default; compare-mode allows selecting two time ranges side-by-side. Model/route filter chips persist across page nav.

Sampling/aggregation trade-off: default backend serves 1m pre-aggregates; when user zooms to <30m window, UI will request raw (or 10s) buckets for high-fidelity view. If raw data unavailable, show note and enable 'request raw now' which triggers on-demand fetch with warning about cost/latency.

Accessibility: All charts must meet 4.5:1 contrast. Provide text-mode summaries for screen readers (pre-computed key metrics). Colorblind palette: use qualitative-safe palette and patterns for heatmap.
Tooltips: include request_id, model, model_version, route, latency percentile values, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_estimate (USD), and a link to trace/PR.
Defaults: Landing view shows 'Top models by cost' and 'Top routes by p95 latency' with quick actions: open route detail, open rollout timeline, set alert based on p95 threshold.
Alerting integration: design exposes quick 'create alert' flow from any chart (pre-populate metric/threshold/aggregation window based on current view).
design_notes: Default persona / flows: 1) SRE investigating a production latency spike; 2) PM comparing two model versions after a rolled update; 3) Platform engineer sizing Dedicated capacity by tokens/sec patterns.
Landing prioritizes routes that contribute >5% of total token cost or have p95 latency above 500ms.
Color use: warm colors (amber/red) for latency/error severity; blue/green for throughput and tokens. Use consistent color mapping across dashboard and route detail.
Prototype decisions: prefer small multiples + heatmap over a single giant matrix to improve scannability for customers with hundreds of routes.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Pre-aggregated 1m rollups reduce query cost but hide short spikes; 2) Raw sampling increases cost and backend complexity. Chosen approach: hybrid with on-demand raw fetch for zoom and trace linking.

Privacy note: tooltips contain request_ids; we must avoid showing actual user prompt text in hover — only prompt length and anonymized example hashes. Security review flagged that trace links must honor PII-redaction policies.
Performance: charts should paginate or lazy-load if >2000 routes. Use server-side top-k for default ranking and client-side filtering for selected subsets.
Export design: CSV includes aggregated metrics, sample trace ids and anonymized example hashes. No raw prompt content exported.
Rollout overlays: show canary allocation percentage and time window; visually tie rollout bands to chart anomalies for quicker causal investigation.
Mobile / responsive: primary metrics collapse into a vertical stack; small multiples become horizontal scrollable carousels. Full heatmap hidden on narrow screens.
Labeling & unit conventions: latency in ms (3 sig figs), throughput in req/s, tokens in tokens/sec, cost in USD with 2 decimal places; show raw counts alongside normalized rates.
Fallback when telemetry gaps: mark chart region with hashed stripe pattern and tooltip that reads 'Telemetry gap: samples unavailable for X minutes'.
review_comments: 2026-02-18 | Priya Desai (PM): Love the small multiples. Request: add a default alert suggestion for any route with p95 > 1s for more than 5m.
2026-02-20 | Ben Chu (Eng - runtime): Backend can provide 1m rollups and 10s raw for the last 30m. We note cost implication for raw fetches; recommend sampling limit when >5k req/s.
2026-02-22 | Lena Hoffmann (Security): Security review required. Confirmed: no prompt text in tooltips/export; ensure trace links require same RBAC checks as console traces.
2026-02-24 | Miguel Ortega (Design owner): Adjusted heatmap color scale and added 'cluster by latency' sorting. Updated small multiples to clip series at 99th percentile to avoid axis explosion.
2026-02-26 | QA (Kofi Mensah): Need acceptance criteria for flakiness: charts should tolerate missing data up to 10% of buckets without full redraw.
2026-02-28 | Alina Ivanov (Accessibility): Request explicit alt-text and text-mode summaries for each chart; confirmed color palette meets contrast after tweak.
2026-03-01 | Miguel Ortega (Assignee): Marking as In Review. Waiting on Eng telemetry contract and Security sign-off to schedule dev work for runtime-1.18.
decisions_and_next_steps: Decision: Implement hybrid aggregation strategy (1m rollups + on-demand raw) and provide a UX affordance for 'request raw now' with cost warning.
Decision: Landing defaults to per-route view; add quick toggle for 'per-model' which reorders the main panels to show model-version heatmap first.
Next step: Eng to write telemetry contract PR with endpoints and rate limits (assigned to ENG-4921).
Next step: Security to complete PII checklist and finalize SSO access gating for trace links (ticket SEC-210).
Next step: PM to add alerting rule templates and update product docs (ticket PM-712).
Next step: Hand-off packet for implementation: Figma frames + chart spec (this doc) + example synthetic dataset and CSV of expected aggregates.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Charts load within 1s for default 24h view with <=10s backend latency; 2) Time-range sync works across panels; 3) Export contains no prompt text; 4) Security sign-off obtained.
